summary: In a Fox News Digital phone interview, actor Jonathan Roumie, who plays Jesus in "The Chosen," discusses his Catholic faith and prayer life and a 25-day Advent prayer challenge on the Hallow app, which he leads with Liam Neeson. He says prayer is easier to build as a habit than people think, and that surrendering to God, as he did five years ago before landing his role, led to peace. He describes the app's Bible readings, music and meditations, and how it has drawn people to prayer and church.
one_line: Jonathan Roumie of "The Chosen" talks about surrender, prayer habits and the Hallow app's 25-day Advent challenge with Liam Neeson.
key_facts: Jonathan Roumie is a Los Angeles-based actor, best known for playing Jesus Christ in "The Chosen," and spoke to Fox News Digital by phone on Monday.
Roumie partnered with Hallow, described as the No. 1 prayer app in the world, for a special Advent prayer challenge for the 2023 season.
The Advent prayer challenge lasts 25 days and began on Monday, the day of the interview.
Roumie and actor Liam Neeson guide people through prayers, meditations, Bible readings and more in the challenge.
Roumie says building a habit of prayer "is easier than people think," and that consistent prayer deepens one's relationship with Jesus and brings more peace, tranquility and serenity.

Roumie says he is easily distracted, and that technology contributes to that, but he is deeply grateful for the Hallow app, which has thousands of prayers and lets him pray or meditate anywhere using headphones.
Roumie says some people who never went to church started going, some who hadn't attended in 20 years returned, and some converted after discovering the app or "The Chosen."
Roumie says the Hallow app is authentically Catholic but is for Christians of all denominations.
Roumie says that five years ago he prayed on his knees, "Jesus, I surrender myself to you. Take care of everything," and three months later he was called to do "The Chosen."
Roumie says trying to micromanage God was not working for him, and that the simple prayer of surrender was the decisive moment that changed everything.
Roumie narrates most of the New Testament in the Hallow app, which also offers music and resources for mental health.
Roumie says playing Jesus has pushed him to examine his own relationship with Him and to deepen his prayer life.
